newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea iron, steel firms mull re-bar output cut.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea iron, steel firms mull re-bar output cut.

text.p: South Korea's iron and steel makers are expected to cut their deformed bar production, also known as reinforcing bars, by 20 percent from October, industry officials said on Wednesday.
"We are considering cutting our deformed bar production by 20 percent starting from next month because of recent high inventories," said an official with Hanbo Steel and General Construction Co Ltd.
An official with the Korea Iron and Steel Association (KISA) said producers' inventories of deformed bar surged to 650,000 tonnes in August from 377,000 tonnes in April and 102,000 tonnes a year ago.
The official said earlier this year, demand had been expected to rise to 10.2 million tonnes this year from 9.2 million tonnes in 1995. However, this may be scaled back.
Kang Won Industries Co Ltd and Korea Iron and Steel Co Ltd were also expected to cut production by 20 percent, traders said.
Inchon Iron and Steel Co Ltd said it preferred raising exports to cutting production.
"We are making every effort to enhance exports instead of cutting our output," said an Inchon Iron official.
"The slowdown in the domestic construction sector has helped manufacturers pile up huge stocks. Most local producers may suffer from carrying cost of record high inventories."
According to a survey by KISA in July, South Korea's exports were seen climbing to more than 300,000 tonnes this year from 105,000 tonnes in 1995.
The Hanbo official said export prices of deformed bar fell to $270 per tonne (FOB) in early September, compared with $300 in the first six months of this year.
South Korea exports its products to Southeast Asia, including the Philippines, Vietnam, Indonesia and also to Iran, he said.
Hanbo's annual reinforcing bar production will reach about two million tonnes this year, he added.
Dong Kuk Steel Mill Co Ltd has not yet decided on a course of action, a spokesman said.
"We have not decided yet whether to cut our production," he said.
"But we are well aware of the current market situation and think a cut in production may be needed to keep a balance in the domestic supply and demand."
"Local steel makers will have a meeting on this matter by the end of September," the Dong Kuk spokesman said.
Another option for reinforcing bar makers would be to boost exports, traders said.
"We are trying more than ever to export our products. We have already completed 55,000 tonnes of export deals for the fourth quarter shipment," the Hanbo official said.
